\newcommand{\SlackSentence}{Relays that are neither primary nor designated backup operate at least \SlackOtherA~ms later than the margin would require, on both feeders. The two minima are equal because on each feeder the smallest slack occurs for a single-line-to-ground fault at a hub terminal, cleared by the hub breaker, during which trunk recloser R2 also operates. Both relays then operate on the definite-time part of their earth characteristics, above 20 times pickup, and their time multipliers are the same on both feeders (0.05 and 0.42). The slack, $\frac{13.5}{19}(0.42-1.2\times0.05)-0.11$~s, therefore does not depend on the fault current.}
\newcommand{\TmsSentence}{With the fixed design's pickups and instantaneous settings kept, separate time multipliers for every state shorten clearing by \TmsOnlyA\,\% and \TmsOnlyB\,\%; the rest of the per-state gain comes from pickups and instantaneous settings matched to each state.}
\newcommand{\FinerSentence}{Finer adaptation is not always faster. Beyond $K=\KbestA$ (33-bus) and $K=\KbestB$ (69-bus) groups the best policy slows down again, and own settings for every state are slower than the best policy found. Each group's pickups and instantaneous settings follow the rules for its own states rather than being optimised, so a smaller group is not guaranteed a faster design; the export-keyed rule on the 33-bus feeder and the time-of-day rule on the 69-bus feeder are even slightly slower than the fixed design (Table~\ref{tab:policies}).}
\newcommand{\InfoTwoSentence}{Because peak-load states are grouped apart from light-load states with no hub charging, either policy needs the clock as well as hub status.}
\newcommand{\ClusterTodSentence}{On the 69-bus feeder, two-cluster $k$-means and two-cluster Ward clustering reproduce the time-of-day rule exactly; this partition is stable (bootstrap adjusted Rand index of 1.00) but no faster than the fixed design.}

\newcommand{\StrongSentence}{A stronger source makes the redesigned fixed design slower (254 to 534~ms on the 33-bus feeder and 354 to 1\,046~ms on the 69-bus feeder with 250~MVA).
